newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end weaker as resources wilt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end weaker as resources wilt.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2236 -13 US 30yr cl 7.11 unch
*Stocks ended lower as major resources issues continued to sag on falling metal prices * Turnover 348.4 million shares, value A$838.0 million, 961 stocks traded, 285 steady, 306 up, 370 down
The Australian share market ended weaker on Thursday, weighed down by major resource issues as investors factored in recent falls and further anticipated falls for base metal prices.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 9.7 points down at 2,236.6, off its intra-session low of 2,227.3.
The September share price index futures closed 13 points down at 2,236, a 0.6 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said negative comments on the outlook for copper and steel prices by BHP managing director John Prescott on Tuesday were still being factored into the market by investors today.
"It has been a mixed day but the underlying theme has been the continuing slide of the big resource companies, BHP and CRA," a Melbourne dealer said.

The dealer said the two bellwether stocks, which both have large weightings in the All Ordinaies index, accounted for most of the market's weakness today and effectively held back the entire resources sector.
"Selling of the majors seemed to slow down a bit this afternoon and we might see a pause in the selling on Friday, especially if the U.S. market holds up tonight," the dealer said.
As on Wednesday, investors were seen switching from resource issues into high yielding stocks with the bank sector benefitting the most.
Of the majors, the Commonwealth and ANZ banks saw the best gains although all the majors were firmer on the day.
After the close of trade the RTZ-CRA group announced a first half net profit of A$714 million and an interim dividend of 20.65 cents.
Troubled electronics group AWA said its year net loss narrowed to A$14.26 million from A$22.16 million and its managing director, John Dougall announced his resignation.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trading was busy with both options and futures responding to the market's downgrading of the resources sector over the last two sessions.
Total options turnover 65,720 (57,133)
Turnover in September futures totalled 10,928 (4,257) -----------------------(TECHNICALS)------------------------- Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20
In other local markets, Australian bonds were up but off early highs ahead of important U.S. inflation to be released later today.
Bonds were whipped around early after the release of the August labour force report which was bullish for the market.
By 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 8.10 percent, down 0.04 from Wednesday's levels.
The Australian dollar bumped along the floor of its recent tight range during the session as the market digested the mixed August jobs data.
By 4.55 p.m.(0655 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7985/95.
